agenda.say:
• Welcome; today starts John Doe's case from the beginning, on the Day 1 deck
• Part 1, the lessons: fundamentals, intake, claim set-up and the Case Plan, the car, client communications, who pays the bills, treatment
• Part 2, the daily loop: meet John Doe on his Case Profile and do his Intake, our Skill Building
• Then 📁 Backup File Maintenance, required: the firm's folders on his Backup Drive; then write the Action Plan
• Then 5 short skill activities in a 25-minute Practice Lab: every trainee works all 5
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 2

lab.say:
• Practice Lab: 5 short skill activities, each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• Intake and claim set-up: John Doe's voicemail and his Direction Packet, the LORs to every carrier
• Care and the client: the Payer Order and the LOPs, the Case Plan with the gap in its risks, the near-drop
• About 25 minutes: time for all 5, about five minutes each; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• Robert Smith's insurer has already called John Doe, and he needs a car for work
• Discuss what to tell him today, in what order
• Cover: the do's and don'ts in plain words and the rental path
• Log every step the same day; route anything legal to Atty. Thorne
• What John says this week stays in the adjuster's notes for the life of the case
wrap.ask: What would you tell John Doe first, and why first?

lifemap.say:
• The whole of John Doe's file on one slide, in the order we work it this week
• Across the top: the seven stages you carry on every file
• Day 1 it's raw: the loss, the SOL docketed, the matter opened in the CMS
• Then claims and care, the demand, liens and ADR, and litigation to the close
• Each day picks the file up where the last one left it
lifemap.ask: Which one date on this track would you protect first, and why?

coverage.say:
• Three layers pay in order: BI $10,000, Host UM $20,000, Relative UM $10,000
• $40,000 is the cap, so the care and records must prove value through all three
• Before any BI release: the UM consent to settle and the subrogation waiver
• The Health Plan pays care now and recovers from the settlement, so plan the reduction early
• The gap before treatment is the weak point: name it on Day 1, with its reason documented
coverage.ask: If the BI adjuster offered the full $10,000 tomorrow, what must be on the file before anyone says yes?

plan.say:
• Step 4 of the loop, guided: the Action Plan template, section by section, on the shared screen
• Every fact from the Intake with the document it comes from; every action item with an owner, a date and a tool
• Anything only Atty. Thorne decides is routed to him, with the date

agenda.say:
• Welcome back; today is the Day 2 deck: pre-demand, the BI demand and the BI settlement
• Lessons: the pre-demand audit, the gap record and causation, the demand, negotiations, the UM/UIM safety check, the settlement documents
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then one Skill Building: the Specials, wages and gap record, then the BI demand served
• Then 📁 Backup File Maintenance, required: today's documents filed the firm's way; then update the Action Plan
• Then 4 short skill activities in a 20-minute Practice Lab: every trainee works all 4
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 3

lab.say:
• Practice Lab: 4 short skill activities, each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The gap call with John Doe, the strategy session with Atty. Thorne
• The offer, the release
• About 20 minutes: time for all 4, about five minutes each; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• 07/20/2026: Specials audited; Atty. Thorne approved a policy-limits demand to Keystone
• Discuss what must be true before the Time-Limited Demand goes out
• Cover: every record and bill included, numbers matching the audit, a clear reasonable deadline, proof of receipt, Atty. Thorne's sign-off
• One missing page lets Keystone argue it never had a fair chance to settle
• Next: the $40,000 gross meets the bills, and how it gets split
wrap.ask: What must be true before the Time-Limited Demand goes out to Keystone?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Treatment is complete: MMI 06/12/2026, Specials $42,984.00, the gap still to be explained from his documents
• Then straight into the Skill Building: the BI demand

plan.say:
• Step 4: update the Action Plan: where the demand stands and the next deadline
• A lighter touch today: the trainees write it, you spot-check two plans

agenda.say:
• Welcome back; today is the Day 3 deck: lien negotiation and disbursement
• Lessons: the lien doctrines and prior-attorney liens, increasing the client's net, the Net Sheet, disbursement, final reconciliation
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then one Skill Building, the final Net Sheet: liens, ledger, then the disbursement
• Then 📁 Backup File Maintenance, required; then update the Action Plan
• Then 4 short skill activities in a 26-minute Practice Lab: time for all 4
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 4

lab.say:
• Practice Lab: 4 short skill activities, each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The two lien reductions, the prior-attorney lien, the BI-alone Net Sheet
• About 26 minutes: time for all 4, about six minutes each; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• 10/21/2026: John Doe's check reads $20,359.92; he expected about $26,000
• Discuss how you walk him through his Net Sheet, line by line
• Cover: the 33⅓% fee, the $486.75 in costs, both liens after their reductions, the two streams
• You explain the figures; the fee and any change to them are Atty. Thorne's call
• Nothing leaves trust before the release is signed and the funds clear
wrap.ask: How do you walk John through his Net Sheet, and what is Atty. Thorne's call, not yours?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Track A settled at $40,000 gross; the liens and the provider balance still to resolve
• Then straight into the Skill Building: the final Net Sheet

plan.say:
• Step 4: update the Action Plan: each lien's status, the Net Sheet and the disbursement date
• A lighter touch today: the trainees write it, you spot-check two plans

agenda.say:
• Welcome back; today is the Day 4 deck: mediation and arbitration, on Track B, where the file doesn't settle
• Lessons: the neutral, mediation logistics, the hearing and its UPL line, court rules and UM disputes, both binders
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then one Skill Building, the Mediation Binder, its calendaring included
• Then 📁 Backup File Maintenance, required; then update the Action Plan
• Then 4 short skill activities in a 20-minute Practice Lab: every trainee works all 4
• Knowledge Check: 70% opens Day 5

lab.say:
• Practice Lab: 4 short skill activities, each one an assumption and one entry to log in the CMS
• The impasse routes, the court cutoffs, the arbitration calendar, a bottleneck
• About 20 minutes: time for all 4, about five minutes each; then the Ready check

wrap.say:
• Track B: the mediation is set for 03/18/2027
• Opposing counsel's paralegal calls to ask what number John Doe will take
• Discuss what you may say and what goes to Atty. Thorne
• Cover: no settlement position and no legal advice from you; log the call; route it the same day
• Every binder exhibit indexed and numbered before the exchange
wrap.ask: What may you say to the paralegal, and what goes to Atty. Thorne the same day?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Track B: the same file, where Keystone let the demand lapse; mediation and UM arbitration ahead
• Then straight into the Skill Building: the Mediation Binder

plan.say:
• Step 4: update the Action Plan: the binder's exchange date and what Atty. Thorne still decides
• The trainees work alone; spot-check that every item has an owner and a date

agenda.say:
• Welcome back to the last day: Litigation and Dropped Cases on John Doe's file
• Lessons, about 30 minutes: the litigation fork and filing, litigation tracking, trial prep, depositions, the award, Dropped Cases
• Part 2, the daily loop: the Case Profile, then the Full Application Practice: about 150 minutes on the assigned companion case, graded on Days 1–4
• Then 📁 Backup File Maintenance, required: the final backup audit; then close out the Action Plan
• John's 3 other Skill Activities are extra practice, each a rehearsal of a companion case's own problem
• Knowledge Check: 70% finishes the Case Flow

lab.say:
• Practice Lab: 3 Skill Activities on John Doe's file in the CMS, extra practice today
• Each rehearses a problem the companion cases raise: pleadings and discovery calendaring, deposition prep, skip-tracing and the certified notice
• Point each trainee to the one that matches their own case's problem (the final backup audit is the required Backup File Maintenance)
• Calendar everything each task starts; in litigation a missed date can end the claim

wrap.say:
• 01/05/2027: opposing counsel's paralegal says discovery responses are late; John Doe changed his number; deposition set 02/18/2027
• Confirm the real discovery deadline on the calendar; tell Atty. Thorne today
• Start outreach on every approved channel and log it; if John stays silent, begin the skip-trace steps
• Protect the deposition date; more time, or what to tell the other side, is Atty. Thorne's call
• Late discovery can cost the client evidence and money
wrap.ask: What do you do today, in what order, and what is Atty. Thorne's call, not yours?

build.say:
• Full Application Practice: the rest of the day, about 150 minutes, building the assigned companion case, worked like John Doe's file
• Step 1, read the file; step 2, open it in the CMS, Conflict Check first on every party's full legal name
• Step 3, the folder by the SOP: [Your Full Name] - [Case Name], nine subfolders, connected, intake documents uploaded
• Step 4, the claims: every carrier in the stack, Letters of Representation, verification status, coverage matrix
• Time is called at each step; each case has its own problem to find
build.ask: What is the first fact on your case to confirm, and where?

extra.say:
• Extra practice: John Doe's 3 other Day 5 Skill Activities, untimed (the final backup audit was the required Backup File Maintenance)
• Today's practical was the companion case
• Worth coming back to soon: the one that matches your own case's problem, calendaring, deposition prep or the skip-trace
• Most rooms skip these: the skip button goes to the Ready check, then the Knowledge Check

build2.say:
• Second half: steps 5 to 7
• Step 5, plan the care: treatment map, 14-day rule and any gap, who pays first, whether an LOP is needed
• LOP, Letter of Protection: the firm's written promise to pay a provider from the settlement
• Step 6, the Case Notes entry for Atty. Thorne: decision first, then the deadline it hangs on
• Step 7, check the work: every document in the CMS and case folder, CMS Case ID logged
build2.ask: What decision does the note to Atty. Thorne lead with?

profile.say:
• Step 2 of the loop: John Doe's Case Profile, The Case So Far
• Track B: the demand lapsed, suit filed 09/24/2026, discovery and the deposition ahead
• Then straight into the Full Application Practice

plan.say:
• Step 4: close out the Action Plan: the litigation handoff, what is still open, the sign-off
• A few minutes, on their own
